This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox.

### Summary

**UPDATE**: I believe the culprit is a bug in the `@st.cache_resource` logic and/or the way streamlit handles db connections that try to persist (had same issues using `session_state`). See my follow-up message below. 

My initial issue:

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

value = st.selectbox(items based on search_input)

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete
def search_files(searchterm):
  refine search based (in part) on value
selected_value = st_combobox(search_files, ...)

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

value = st.selectbox(items based on search_input)

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete
def search_files(searchterm):
  refine search based (in part) on value
selected_value = st_combobox(search_files, ...)

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded
uses st.experimental_set_query_params at some point
no database or complex cached stuff
...

# make plotly plot(s) here
```

Unfortunately I'm not able to figure out exactly why this happens. It doesn't seem to happen consistently. 

However, often I see this error nearby: `2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query`.

```
@st.cache_resource

    creds = ...
    dbconn = SQL("EXAMPLE", "example.com", creds["username"], creds["password"], True)
    return dbconn
```

I expect this crash not to happen.

```
free(): double free detected in tcache 2
Aborted
```

Sometimes I see this error too (maybe it's related to the cache_resource having issues?):
```
2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query
```
This error doesn't seem to crash outright, but something tells me it's related.

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04
- Browser: Brave Version 1.57.62, Chromium: 116.0.5845.180 (Official Build) (64-bit)

I'm going to be trying to nail down exactly why this issue is happening over the next few days (try to figure out how to reproduce it) but I wanted to make the issue now since it seems like a very strange error someone on the team might have insight into.

When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. Cached objects are stored in "pickled" form, which means that the return
value of a cached function must be pickleable. Each caller of the cached
function gets its own copy of the cached data.

This process of serializing and deserializing the cached object creates a copy of our original DataFrame. While this copying behavior may seem unnecessary, it's what we want when caching data objects since it effectively prevents mutation and concurrency issues. Read the section “[Mutation and concurrency issues](#mutation-and-concurrency-issues)" below to understand this in more detail.

Ensure your cached functions return trusted values because it is possible to construct malicious pickle data that will execute arbitrary code during unpickling. Never load data that could have come from an untrusted source in an unsafe mode or that could have been tampered with. **Only load data you trust**.

summary.problem:
st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```
